chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: A Bedouin man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'I dwell in the desert, so teach me the comprehensive words.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I order you not to get angry.' The Bedouin reiterated the question to him three times, until the man returned to himself and said, 'I shall not ask about anything after this. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not order me except with good.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And my father used to say: What is more difficult than anger? Indeed, when a man gets angry, he kills the soul which Allah has prohibited, and he slanders the married woman.'

key_terms.جَوَامِعَ الْكَلَامِ: comprehensive words / key principles of speech

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) teach as the comprehensive words for a Bedouin man?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the Prophet’s concise advice to a Bedouin to 'not get angry,' emphasizing its repetition to underscore its centrality in comprehensive knowledge. The Imam elaborates on the severity of anger by linking it to two major sins: self-destruction (often interpreted as death from rage or homicide) and slander of chaste women, illustrating how a single vice can lead to multiple spiritual and social corruptions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, said, ‘

I heard my<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> father<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> saying: ‘A Bedouin man came over to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and he said, ‘I dwell in the desert, so teach me the comprehensive words’. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> order you that you should not get angry’. So the Bedouin reiterated the question upon him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> three times, until the man retracted it to himself and he said, ‘I shall not ask about anything after this. Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> did not order me except with the good’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And my<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> father<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> was saying: ‘Which thing is more difficult than the anger. Once the man gets angry so he kills the soul which Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> has Prohibited and he slanders the married woman’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“I heard my father saying, ‘Once a Bedouin man came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “1 live in the Sahara, please teach me comprehensive words of advice.” The Messenger of Allah said, ‘I command you not to become angry.’ The man from the desert repeated his question three times. He then realized the fact and said, ‘I will not ask for anything hereinafter. The Messenger of Allah has commanded me nothing but good. ’

The Imam said, ‘My father has said, “What can be more severe (in harmfulness) than anger? A man becomes angry, he commits murder that is unlawful and accuses a married woman of committing indecent acts.’””
